items.stem: In a CPM network, what defines the critical path?

options.text: The longest path of activities with the least total float, determining project duration
options.rationale: Correct: the critical path is the longest path with minimum float and sets the project's finish date.

options.text: The path with the most activities regardless of duration
options.rationale: Activity count does not define criticality; duration and float do.

options.text: The path with the highest cost
options.rationale: Cost does not define the critical path.

options.text: Any path chosen by the scheduler
options.rationale: The critical path is derived from the network logic, not chosen arbitrarily.

items.explanation: Correct: the critical path is the longest path with minimum float and sets the project's finish date.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An activity has total float of 5 days. What does this mean?

options.text: It can be delayed up to 5 days without delaying project completion
options.rationale: Correct: total float is the time an activity can slip without delaying the project finish.
Float measures allowable delay, not a required early start.

options.text: It will always finish 5 days late
options.rationale: Float is available slack, not a guaranteed delay.

options.text: It has no effect on the schedule ever
options.rationale: If delayed beyond its float, it would affect the schedule.

items.explanation: Correct: total float is the time an activity can slip without delaying the project finish.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate techniques to shorten a schedule's duration? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: fast-tracking overlaps activities to compress duration, accepting some risk.

options.text: Crashing by adding resources to critical activities
options.rationale: Correct: crashing adds resources to reduce critical-path durations, usually at added cost.
Extending durations lengthens, not shortens, the schedule.

options.text: Removing the baseline to hide slippage
options.rationale: Deleting the baseline does not shorten the schedule and undermines control.

options.text: Increasing total float on non-critical paths
options.rationale: Changing non-critical float does not shorten overall project duration.

items.explanation: Correct: fast-tracking overlaps activities to compress duration, accepting some risk.
